content.title: Red Lions edge Blue Sharks in extra-time thriller
paragraphs: Red Lions beat Blue Sharks 3-2 after extra time in a match that swung back and forth. Fox put Red Lions ahead in the 28th minute, Gray levelled for Blue Sharks in the 62nd, Reid restored the lead in the 95th, Cruz brought Blue Sharks back at 105 minutes, and Bell scored at 113 minutes to make it 3-2.

The numbers show Red Lions carried the greater share of the game. Red Lions finished with 69 possession, 85 field tilt, 110 final-third entries and 27 shots, compared with Blue Sharks on 31 possession, 15 field tilt, 31 final-third entries and 15 shots. Red Lions also had 6 big chances to Blue Sharks’ 5, and Blue Sharks spent much more of the match defending deep.

The late stages were messy and tense, with the last 10 minutes described as chaotic. Red Lions still had 91 field tilt and 79 possession in that spell, which underlined how much of the play was in Blue Sharks’ end before the match ended at 120+1'.

draft.title: Red Lions edge Blue Sharks in extra-time thriller
paragraphs: Red Lions won 3 to 2 after extra time in a match that swung back and forth from start to finish. Fox put Red Lions ahead in the 28th minute, Gray levelled for Blue Sharks on 62 minutes, Reid restored the lead in the 95th minute, and Cruz brought Blue Sharks back at 105 minutes before Bell’s own goal in the 113th minute settled the score.

Red Lions controlled the game for long spells and did most of the ball work, finishing with 69 possession, 85 field tilt and 110 entries into the final third, while Blue Sharks were forced deeper and ended on 31 possession and 15 field tilt. Red Lions also created more, with 27 shots and 6 big chances compared with 15 shots and 5 big chances, but the finishing was wasteful on both sides.

The turning point came in extra time, when Red Lions kept pinning Blue Sharks back and kept asking the harder questions in the box. Even in a chaotic last stretch, Red Lions stayed on the front foot long enough to finally get over the line.
